question: Do evildoers prosper?
summary: Job 12:6 says the tents of robbers prosper and those who provoke God are secure. Psalm 73:3-7, 12 describes the prosperity of the wicked at length — they are not in trouble, they wear pride as a necklace, they increase in riches. Jeremiah 12:1 asks why the way of the wicked prospers. Against this, Psalm 34:21 says evil shall slay the wicked and those who hate the righteous shall be desolate. The biblical wisdom and poetic tradition contains both empirical observations that evil prospers and theological assertions that it does not.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers distinguish the wicked's present, temporary prosperity from their final ruin, so the observation that evil prospers and the assertion that it perishes describe different stages of one outcome.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells sets the texts that say the wicked prosper (Job 12:6; Ps 73; Jer 12:1) against those that say evil destroys them (Ps 34:21) as flatly contradictory answers.

pd_work.note: On Job 12:6 Henry grants that robbers' tents prosper now but argues God reserves the exact distribution of rewards and punishments for the future state, the standard harmonizing reading of the wisdom tension.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why do the wicked prosper?
link.note: Engages Psalm 73, Job, and Jeremiah 12:1 directly, arguing the wicked's prosperity is fleeting against their eternal judgment, the temporary-vs-final reading.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The godly might suffer, but the Lord will reward them in the end. Similarly, the wicked might prosper for a time, but ultimately they will perish (1:6; 34:15-16).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The cleanest temporary-vs-final harmonization: the wicked prosper 'for a time' (Job/Ps 73/Jer) yet 'ultimately perish' (Ps 34:21), so both poles describe different stages of one outcome.
